title: Routing Architecture
content:
Photon uses an efficient routing system with a radix tree data structure for fast route matching. Routes are registered when you define them, and the router builds an optimized tree structure for matching.

Routing Architecture

The router uses a radix tree (also known as a trie) for route matching. This provides:

  • Fast Static Route Matching: Static routes are matched efficiently.
  • Dynamic Parameter Extraction: Route parameters like :id are extracted during matching.
  • Wildcard Support: Support for wildcard routes like /api/*.

Route Registration

Routes are registered when you call methods like app.get() or app.post():

const app = new Photon()

// Routes are registered immediately
app.get('/users', handler)
app.get('/users/:id', handler)
app.post('/users', handler)

// The router builds an optimized tree structure
// for efficient matching at request time
